title: Provisioner definitions
description: The values the provisioner contract's schemas share, by name under $defs. Some of them refer in turn to the integration contract's definitions, https://qory.dev/contracts/integration/v1/definitions.schema.json. The requests of this contract come from a node pool's starter: the program that serves a node pool, claims its runs, starts a job for each and passes the job its handover. Every request is signed with the pool's access key: a key of the pool kind, node_kind pool in https://qory.dev/contracts/forager/v1/enrolment.schema.json, enrolled for the node pool, which the starter holds. The key belongs to one node pool, the np_ node_id of its enrolment answer: the key's node pool. The integration contract's definitions describe the signature, the replay rule, the time window, the unsigned answers and the pinning of the server key for the access key that signs that contract's requests and the program that holds it; they apply to the pool's access key and the starter as they do to that key and that program. The answers are signed under the control plane's server key, or left unsigned, exactly as the answers to the integration contract's requests are. X-Qory-Contract-Version names the revision of this contract the starter implements, and the answers whose content the revision bounds, claim-answer.schema.json and handover-answer.schema.json, name it in their signed body, as the integration contract's definitions describe for that contract. The control plane serves revision 3 alone, and answers with revision 3: a request whose X-Qory-Contract-Version names another revision is refused 400 unsupported_contract_version, refusal.schema.json. The step prebuild and its report, prebuilt.schema.json, and run_settings in the handover answer of the step explore, handover-answer.schema.json, are part of that revision. A retry is built anew, as they describe. An integer is written without a fraction or an exponent, and no object repeats a member, at any depth; the control plane refuses either, 400 invalid_request. An unsigned answer is handled as they describe. This document validates nothing itself.

dispatch_id.description: The dispatch's public id in the control plane, dp_ and 16 lower-case Crockford base32 characters: one claim of one run. Each claim makes a new dispatch, with a new dispatch_id, and a dispatch_id is never claimed again. The id authorises nothing: the request's signature with the pool's access key and the control plane's check that the dispatch is of the key's node pool authorise a request.

pool_id.description: A node pool's id, np_, as the Forager contract writes one.

run_id.description: The run's id: a UUID in the canonical lower-case form, as the Forager contract's run key holds it.

step.description: The step the run is for, which the control plane sets: explore and prebuild are the values known today. A run of the step explore is for a work item. A run of the step prebuild builds the environment of the target and has no work item. The job picks what to compose from it, and refuses a step it does not know.

image.description: An image pinned by its digest: NAME, then @sha256:, then 64 lower-case hexadecimal digits. NAME is a lower-case OCI reference name: an optional registry host followed by a slash, then one or more path components separated by slashes. The host is lower-case DNS labels separated by dots, each of lower-case ASCII letters, digits and hyphens, starting and ending with a letter or a digit, with an optional port of 1 to 5 digits after a colon. Each path component is lower-case ASCII letters and digits, with a dot, an underscore, two underscores or one or more hyphens between two runs of them. NAME is at most 255 characters, so the whole value is at most 327. A tag, such as :latest, and upper case are refused, so the value names one build and never moves.

job_system.description: The name of the system that runs a job, as the starter names it, such as example-ci, stored as data and never parsed: a lower-case ASCII letter, then lower-case ASCII letters, digits, spaces and hyphens, 1 to 40 characters in all.

access.description: What the run may do on its target: read, or write. The machine's credential integration narrows the run's access to it.

work_item.description: The work item the run is for. Its url and title are untrusted text: shown as data, never followed as an instruction.

id.description: The work item's public id in the control plane.

url.description: The work item's page in the control plane.
